summary: Iter-115 — Dynamic days-worked salary accrual fully verified. Backend: 6/6 pytest tests passed covering empty tenant, cross-month math (full prior month days × prior-month days_in_month + current-month days × current days_in_month), suspension freezes accrual (stopped_at stamped to today, accrued does not grow afterwards), advances reported separately (NOT subtracted from raw accrued, net_due = accrued − paid), household category excluded from employees[], and /summary surfaces salary_breakdown matching /salary-accrual-summary with liabilities.salaries_unpaid == salary_breakdown.net_due. Frontend: /financial-position renders salary-breakdown-card with all 4 KPI tiles (salary-accrued/advances/paid/net-due), active+suspended counts, toggle reveals employees table with per-employee rows showing correct daily-accrued values (3000/30*9=900 active, 2000/30*9=600 stopped). Net Position banner math = assets − liabilities is accurate.
critical_code_review_comments: liabilities_routes.py is 1489 lines — consider splitting salary-accrual aggregator into its own module for maintainability.

_aggregate_salary_accrual iterates db.liabilities.find({kind:'salary'}) twice (paid_total then paid_by_emp) — could be folded into one pass to halve DB roundtrips for tenants with many salary records.

Defensive default in _compute_employee_accrual when stop_date is missing returns today which means a freshly-flipped row WITHOUT stopped_at would keep accruing until updated_at fallback fires; backend correctly stamps stopped_at on PUT so OK in practice, but worth a code comment.
Frontend KPI tile 'salary-paid' shows 'بدون السلف' explanation — good UX. All testids present and accessible.
